            Image output

            2592 × 1944

            Image size

            The one size everything else is derived from. The sensor always reads the full frame; every output below is downscaled from it and never larger. Smaller sizes cost much less CPU and reduce noise and file size.

            --Live view
            --Analysis
            --Archive

            Live view

            75

            Sums each star's light over an N×N window above the sky background (stars ~N² brighter, noise only ~N×). Only the live view and snapshots, only while the sun is below −6° and only inside the sky mask; star count, cloud cover and archived frames are unchanged.

            Star count & cloud cover

            Stars are counted only at night. Each sample is plotted under Live → Cloud cover history. A smaller analysis width is much cheaper on CPU.

            Capture timing

            Raise these if the computer runs hot; exposures longer than the interval are not affected.

            White balance

            Applies to RAW10 frames (night, or exposure ≥ 0.4 s) and as a gentle correction on top of the camera ISP in MJPG mode (daytime).

            Camera

            --

            Camera

            Choose which attached camera Zenivo uses (ZWO ASI, IMX335 USB, Raspberry Pi camera, webcam). The choice is used at the next start unless --camera is given. Switching pauses capture for a few seconds.

            Detection

            Events

            Streaks and flashes are looked for at night only (sun below −8°) on a 640 px gray copy of each new frame compared with the previous one. A streak in a single frame is a meteor; a dashed one or one continuing in the next frame is an aircraft (faint and steady: a satellite). Cloud changes reuse the cloud cover samples, so they need “Star count & cloud cover” on. Set a sky mask to ignore roads and windows. Events are listed under Archive.

            Cloud cover region

            Only this part of the frame is analysed: exclude buildings, trees and the horizon (e.g. bottom 40% if the lower part shows rooftops). The clear-sky reference is learned automatically; reset it after moving or re-aiming the camera.

            Clear-sky reference

            Daytime objects

            By day a small dark or bright dot that moves against the sky is followed across frames and classified from its size, speed and wing-beat flicker. Rain on the dome pauses recording. The frame interval by day (Image output) sets what can be caught: insects and fast birds need under a second.

            Advanced

            Sizes are in pixels at 640 px frame width. Contrast is how far an object must differ from the sky behind it; empty uses the value of the chosen sensitivity.

            Station & optics

            NOT SOLVED YET

            Location

            Locate via GPS / IP

            When on, a frame, the station coordinates and the time are sent to this server to solve the plate (virtuallab3d.com). Choose Off to send nothing. Without GPS, Locate sends your public IP address to a geolocation service.

            Sensor & lens

            The station clock, observing day and file names follow this timezone.

            Lens & optics

            Mounting

            Optical center and angles use native sensor coordinates; the sky overlay applies mirror/flip automatically.

            Refined from star matches by plate-solving (AUTO).

            Plate solve

            Plate-solving on a starry night measures the lens and mounting parameters and saves them automatically, as does Locate for the coordinates. Fields you edit by hand are saved as soon as you leave them.

            Ignore the saved lens: re-read the sensor and re-measure focal length, distortion and optical centre from a 90 s star-tracking series (clear night). The old values are kept if the solve fails.

            Sky mask

            Outline open sky

            Press Auto-detect to propose the mask from the current frame (best at night), or tap the frame to outline open sky (green) and lit buildings, trees or poles to ignore (red). Nothing is stored until you press Apply, so you can fix the proposal first. The plate solver only uses stars inside the sky and outside obstructions, on top of its own automatic sky detection.

            Align by stars

            For when the automatic solve is wrong. Tap 4 or more stars you can really see on the open sky (inside the green outline), spread over the frame, brightest first. The solver identifies them from their mutual angles, shows the result, and only stores it when you press Apply.

            Integrations

            ADS-B receiver

            With a local ADS-B receiver (dump1090, readsb or a Flightradar24 feeder: BaseStation port 30003), each aircraft event is matched to the flight whose position, projected with the star-solved camera pointing, lies on the streak. A “meteor” that matches a flight becomes an aircraft. The feed is only read at night while aircraft detection is on.

            Off by default. When on, this station sends the aircraft positions your receiver decoded (public broadcast data) to the Zenivo network server (the origin of your remote solver URL; nothing is sent while that is empty), signed with this station’s key, every 5 s while your receiver delivers. The server sees this station’s IP address and can estimate where your receiver is from what it hears. Data from adsb.fi, adsb.lol or Flightradar24 is never forwarded.

            Public ADS-B network
            Privacy

            Off by default. Used only while your receiver is missing, not connected, or silent for more than 90 s; polling stops as soon as it is back. When on, this station sends its position rounded to 0.5 degree (about 55 km), in this order: to the Zenivo network (only if a remote solver URL is set), then to adsb.fi, and to adsb.lol; the next one is used when one fails or returns no aircraft for 2 minutes. The data is for personal, non-commercial use.

            Flightradar24

            Privacy

            Off by default. When on, this station asks flightradar24.com for the aircraft positions around it; without credentials the public feed is used. Credentials are stored on this station only (token and e-mail in data/station_config.json, the password in memory only, never shown again). This uses Flightradar24’s web endpoints, which are not an official public API. You are responsible for using it within Flightradar24’s terms; a subscription token is the supported way for account holders.

            Weather balloons (SondeHub)
            Privacy

            When on, the station asks api.v2.sondehub.org for the weather balloons within 350 km, about every 20 s while a Live page is open. The position sent is rounded to 0.5° (about 55 km); the exact location never leaves this station.

            Satellites

            When on, the station asks celestrak.org for orbit data (no position is sent). Satellites are computed locally; a long list slows the live view on a small host, so keep only the groups you want to see.

            SatNOGS (db.satnogs.org) is an open, volunteer-run satellite database. It serves one file with every satellite, about 250 KB per download, so the groups below do not apply. Only the request itself is sent, never a position.

            Weather & forecast

            Off by default. When on, the station asks api.open-meteo.com (free, no account) for the weather at its position, rounded to 0.1° (about 11 km); no name, address or picture is sent. Same data at GET /api/weather.

            Community

            Shares the station name, an approximate location and, if enabled, a small preview image with other Zenivo stations. Anyone can see it. It is off until you turn it on. The location is rounded as set under Admin → Public location.

            Enlarging the preview and the map link need a public URL (up to 1280 px). Turning the link off only removes it from the community map; whoever knows the address can still open the station, as before.

            On by default. This station then stores and serves large preview images sent by stations without a public address (re-encoded JPEG, at most 1280 px, up to 100 stations and 25 MB, kept 24 hours). Turning it off deletes everything held and refuses new uploads.

            Needs sharing on. Messages pass through hub stations (chat on and a public address): public-room messages are readable by anyone, private messages are end-to-end encrypted, but hubs can see who talks to whom and when. Turning it off stops all chat traffic and deletes what this station held for others; your own history stays.

            Seeds

            One URL per line. Stations asked first in every round. The built-in ones are listed and can be removed; with an empty list this station only talks to stations it already knows.

              Starts focus mode by itself, then sweeps the lens to find the sharpest position.
               
              Autofocus options
               
              Exposure

              Auto-exposure pauses in focus mode so the score stays comparable. If the light changed, meter once. Short exposures refresh faster and blur less.

              How to focus

              • Aim at a bright star near the centre (or a distant light by day), then press Start.
              • Move the lens until the star size drops or the score rises; the star marks the sharpest position.
              • Press Finish to keep the lens position and leave focus mode.
